title: Hotpath small-batch attention kernel calibration and canary plan
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: We have intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes for short prompt workloads (<64 tokens) on the hosted fleet when the runtime selects FlashAttention v3 under small microbatch conditions. Root cause is likely a mismatch between kernel startup overhead and decode prefill pacing when microbatch size < 8 and sequence length distribution is skewed to short contexts.

Goal: Calibrate kernel selection thresholds and prefill/decode pacing policies to reduce 95th/99th tail latency for short-prompt, low-concurrency requests while preserving throughput and cost. Produce a guarded canary rollout with observable rollback criteria.

Scope: runtime kernel scorer and policy config, telemetry instrumentation for microbatch heatmaps, synthetic workload prober, lightweight canary in staging and small percentage of hosted traffic. No model format changes.

Hypotheses: 1) v3 achieves better avg tokens/sec but has fixed startup overhead that dominates short decode when microbatch < 8; 2) small-batch heuristics should bias towards v2 (or v3 with warmup) unless request burst/seq distribution indicates sustained throughput; 3) a quick prefill-delay (5-15ms) during startup for microbatch<8 will eliminate oscillation without harming tail for larger batches.

Planned work items:
- Implement instrumentation: per-request microbatch_size, seq_len, selected_kernel, kernel_start_us, first_token_latency_us (telemetry tags). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Hotpath+Kernel+Calibration
- Add a runtime policy knob: 'small_batch_bias' threshold and 'startup_warm_delay_ms' applied only for kernel switch decisions on first decode loop.
- Build synthetic prober that replays short-prompt traffic at controlled concurrency to exercise selection logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/kernel-prober
- Run A/B in staging: compare default policy vs calibrated policy across latency percentiles and cost-per-token.
- Canary rollout plan for hosted: 0.5% → 2% → 8% traffic with automatic rollback on SLO breach (95th tail increase >10% absolute or error rate >0.1%).

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th and 99th tail latency for short-prompt cohort (<64 tokens) reduces by at least 20% in staging tests without increasing mean latency by >5% for long-prompt cohort (>256 tokens).
- No increase in user-visible error rate or throttling events during canary.
- Telemetry shows decreased kernel flip rate for affected workloads.
- Rollout automation and alerting configured and tested.

Success metrics (measured over 24h canary window):
- 99th latency delta (short cohort) <= -20% relative to baseline
- Kernel handoff events per 1k requests reduced by >=30% for small-batch flows
- Cost delta (per-token GPU time) within +/-5%

Rollout & rollback rules:
- Auto roll forward on each window if no alerts and SLA metrics pass.
- Immediate rollback if error_rate > 0.1% OR 95th latency for short cohort increases by >10% absolute OR anomalies in kernel_start_us > 2x baseline.

Notes about trade-offs: aggressive bias to v2 reduces tail but may raise unit cost for larger bursts; warm-delay increases single-request latency slightly but stabilizes kernel choice. We aim for minimal user impact while improving SLOs for latency-sensitive use cases.
